rationale:
Round-2 duty: re-verify the round-1 fix commits (0d21cb26 code + 0783a507 docs, diffed against my round-1 tip 8eaeb05e) don't regress my regression-hunt basis (release, reconcile-mode complete, impl adopt, repair phase, spec create, plan approve). Confirmed clean — every change touching my basis is either (a) a pure render-sink escaping fix (G3/G4, next.RenderBDError / strconv.Quote-on-recovery-line-shaped-text) with no behavioral effect on values written or derived, or (b) the two substantive fixes the team lead flagged (G1 marker attestation, G2 derive-fallback propagation), both of which I traced end-to-end and found narrowly scoped, well-tested, and non-regressive to the six named workflows.

G1 (marker provenance attestation, internal/complete/materialize.go): adds a new bd-metadata write (`stageMarkerAttestationKey`) immediately before each write-ahead marker publish, and gates both discriminator resume legs on the attestation matching the observed marker OID (mismatch/absent -> FOREIGN -> clear -> normal fully-gated run). This only fires inside `resolveMaterializationDiscriminator`, which is guarded by `if reconcile == nil` in complete.go -- reconcile mode is structurally untouched by this change, exactly as the round-1 diff's own comment states ("Reconcile mode is UNCHANGED"). Covered by 6 new tests in materialize_attestation_test.go (resume-with-attestation, unattested-clears, mismatched-clears, read-failure-propagates, the parent-leg-never-advances-branch-on-forgery case, and a seam-defaults test) plus the R6-executed spoof repro re-verified as leg (xxiv) in bead6_fixture_legs_test.go, which now properly round-trips its bd-metadata fake through an in-memory map (fault_injection_realgit_test.go) rather than a real bd process -- this is fully hermetic, unlike the one real-bd release test I flagged as a minor finding in round 1. The disclosed pre-fix in-flight-marker migration note (ADR-0041 lines ~397-412: an attestation-less marker from a binary predating this fix classifies FOREIGN on first post-upgrade encounter, clears, and falls back to one normal fully-gated run) is a safe one-time degrade -- never a false resume, never lost/corrupted state -- and does not touch release, repair phase, adopt, spec create, or plan approve at all. Acceptable as characterized.

G2 (derive-fallback propagation, internal/phase/derive.go): a failed `bd list`-backed child read now propagates as an error from DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache/DiscoverActiveSpecsWithCache (previously silently swallowed via `children, _ := c.GetChildren(...)`, which fed a nil set into DerivePhaseFromChildren and fabricated a phase such as `plan`), and deriveFromChildrenOrStatusWithCache (the AC-5(iv) consistency-check helper) now returns "" on such a failure so the downstream comparison is skipped rather than asserting a false divergence. This ONLY changes behavior on the error branch (cerr != nil) -- the success path used by ordinary repair-phase/release-sync/plan-approve runs is byte-identical to round 1. Verified this directly: repair.go's own hasDoneMarkerWithCache short-circuit (the branch TestRepairPhase_TerminalRowClosedDoneMarkerAllClosedChildren exercises) returns before reaching the children read at all, so that round-1-caught regression fix is unaffected. New coverage: 4 named tests in derive_swallow_test.go (TestDerivePhase_NoStoredPhase_ChildReadFailurePropagates, TestDerivePhase_ClosedEpicNoDoneMarker_ChildReadFailurePropagates, TestDerivePhase_StoredPhase_ChildReadFailureSkipsConsistencyWarning, TestDiscoverActiveSpecs_ChildReadFailurePropagates) map exactly onto the described fix.

Live verification at tip 0783a507: `go build ./...` clean. All 17 hermetic cmd/mindspec release+repair-phase tests pass fast (TestReleaseOrdering*, TestReleaseDirty*, TestReleaseBeadStateSetOpen, TestReleaseCursorRewindOnlyWhenActive, TestReleaseDefaultSetOpenArgs, TestReleaseSyncPhase_LockTimeoutSurfacedNotDiscarded, and all 9 TestRepairPhase_* tests including the terminal-row regression guard). A full `go test -short ./internal/approve/... ./internal/complete/... ./internal/next/... ./internal/phase/...` run was launched but did not finish within this session due to the same severe multi-reviewer resource contention on this shared worktree noted in round 1 (12 concurrent panel slots running their own go test/bd processes); I rely on the round-1 clean pass of these same packages at 8eaeb05e (exit 0, ~438s/219s/139s/21s) plus this round's narrow, test-verified diff and the fast hermetic subset as sufficient confirmation given the limited scope of change.

select.go/beads.go changes in this round (G4/G7) are message-text and doc-comment-only (dropping a dynamic operand from backtick-fenced command examples, restructuring the ambiguous-match error to name real candidate IDs instead of a templated example) -- the underlying match/ambiguity resolution logic is unchanged; pre-existing tests (TestSelectWorkByName_NamedNotInSet, TestSelectWorkByName_SuffixNotInSet, TestSelectWorkByName_AmbiguousShortFormErrors) still target the same functions and would only need assertion-text updates, not new coverage.

No regression found. Confirming my round-1 basis holds at the round-2 tip.

findings.description: Carried over from round 1, unchanged: bead.MergeMetadata/GetMetadata still exec the real `bd` CLI with no context timeout on the release-sync path (cmd/mindspec/release_test.go's TestReleaseSyncPhase_WriteFailureSurfacedWithConvergentRecovery deliberately does this). G1's new attestation writes add two more such calls per normal complete run, but those are now hermetically faked in the complete-package test suite (fault_injection_realgit_test.go's in-memory attest map), so the exposure is unchanged from round 1, not worsened. Same non-blocking recommendation stands: a follow-up bead to add a context deadline to bd subprocess calls.
